roster_wide_drop_feasibility.rule: The drop candidate for an upside claim is the lowest forward-looking NONSTARTER on the roster, roster-wide - it does NOT need to share the added player's nominal position or role space. A dead or configuration-ineligible bench body is therefore droppable for any legal add. The add must itself be legal (eligible for at least one actual lineup slot) and the post-swap roster/lineup must remain feasible: the number of fillable starting slots may not decrease.
roster_wide_drop_feasibility.nonstarter_feasibility_note: removing a nonstarter can never reduce lineup coverage (the lineup did not use it) and adding a body can never reduce it either, so every nonstarter drop is feasible by construction; the explicit feasibility check binds on started-body drops
roster_wide_drop_feasibility.started_body_rule: a STARTED body is replaceable only when no feasible nonstarter drop exists (an empty bench), and only when the post-swap lineup still fills at least as many slots - this is exactly K/DST streaming and it forbids dropping the only body a slot can use
roster_wide_drop_feasibility.determinism: candidates ordered by (believed projection, index); strict inequalities on both gates; ties never transact
roster_wide_drop_feasibility.replaces: v1/v2's role-space restriction on drop candidates (the C02A rule), which the C02A review found narrower than the required roster-wide opportunity cost
